messages.subject: inla.program has crashed error.
parts:
Hi, 

I recently try to use INLA to fit LGCP. But when I first download it and try to see if it can work on your test sample. I just got the crashed error.  Below is the code and the error message. I hope you can help me about this.

library(INLA)
n = 100; a = 1; b = 1; tau = 100
z = rnorm(n)
eta = a + b*z

scale = exp(rnorm(n))
prec = scale*tau
y = rnorm(n, mean = eta, sd = 1/sqrt(prec))

data = list(y=y, z=z)
formula = y ~ 1+z
result = inla(formula, family = "gaussian", data = data)

summary(result)

Error message: 
readlink: illegal option -- f
usage: readlink [-n] [file ...]
/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/4.3-arm64/Resources/library/INLA/bin/mac.arm64/inla.run: line 65: ./: is a directory
/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/4.3-arm64/Resources/library/INLA/bin/mac.arm64/inla.run: line 71: /Users/--/R data/NARW/: is a directory
/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/4.3-arm64/Resources/library/INLA/bin/mac.arm64/inla.run: line 71: exec: /Users/--/R data/NARW/: cannot execute: Undefined error: 0
Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed() :
  The inla-program exited with an error. Unless you interupted it yourself, please rerun with verbose=TRUE and check the output carefully.
  If this does not help, please contact the developers at <he...@r-inla.org>.

 *** inla.core.safe:  inla.program has crashed: rerun to get better initial values. try=1/1 

Does this mean my environment has some problem or something else? What should I do to prevent this crash problem? Thanks so much for your help. Looking forward to your reply.
